What types of properties are available at Amaya?
Amaya is a 1-million-square-meter master-planned community by Dar Global in central Jeddah. In addition to completed villas and custom land plots, Amaya offers townhouses, mid-to-high-rise residential and commercial plots, and branded or serviced residences, including Trump Plaza.
Is Jeddah good for property investment?
Jeddah is one of Saudi Arabia's largest and most active real estate markets, driven by its status as a commercial hub and gateway city on the Red Sea coast. Demand for residential property in Jeddah is supported by a growing population, ongoing infrastructure investment, and ambitious national development plans under Saudi Vision 2030. Villas and land plots, like those offered at
, tend to appeal to buyers seeking long-term ownership and the option to customize their homes. For buyers considering the Gulf Cooperation Council region, Jeddah offers a relatively stable entry point into a maturing property market with room for continued growth.

Amaya sits in a prime central location along King Abdulaziz Road, directly opposite the Red Sea Mall and minutes from the Jeddah Corniche. This gives buyers a coastal lifestyle address with direct connectivity to key urban and historic hubs.

Amaya offers full freehold ownership options for foreign buyers. Additionally, qualifying real estate investments at Amaya may enable eligible international buyers to apply for the Saudi Premium Residency.
What amenities are near Amaya?
In addition to nearby schools, medical clinics, and mosques, Amaya features signature community amenities. These include a 700-meter central parkland, shaded green walking trails, integrated retail courtyards, and the 4,000-square-meter members-only Vitality Club.

title: Helping Saudi homegrown brands list in London - DarGlobal
text:
03/01/2024
The $72m IPO aims to help Dar Global become a top 50 global developer.
Dar Global, the luxury international real estate developer, started trading on the London Stock Exchange (LSE) on February 28, and became one of the first Saudi homegrown brands to list on the LSE’s main market.
Ziad El Chaar, CEO of Dar Global, says: “We have seen a lot of encouragement from the Ministry of Investment in Saudi Arabia to spread brands overseas. Our initial public offering (IPO) definitely created a lot of news … so many more companies may consider this route.”
Dar Global was established as the international development subsidiary of the Dar Al Arkan Real Estate Development Company, which listed on the Saudi Stock Exchange in 2007. The restructuring process to set up a separate company took almost 10 months. However, Mr El Chaar says preparing for the transaction was a straightforward process as the parent company is already public and has a high degree of governance.

title: Helping Saudi homegrown brands list in London - DarGlobal
text:
Chaar says preparing for the transaction was a straightforward process as the parent company is already public and has a high degree of governance.
Dar Global aspires to become a top-50 developer globally, outside China, and therefore desired to go public on one of the biggest international stock markets. As Mr El Chaar explains, Dar Global wanted the high profile of a London listing and to be subject to English law, which encourages future investment and growth in one of the biggest international property markets.
“We understand the value of joint ventures to expand internationally, and they need development agreements under international laws and a structure that facilitates institutional funding,” he says.
Being a young company, Dar Global chose a private placement and a direct listing that allowed its parent to sell shares, rather than having to issue new stock as in a traditional IPO. The transaction raised $72m in gross proceeds at the placement price of $3.33 per share, valuing Dar Global at around $600m, with Liberum Capital acting as capital markets adviser.

From the supersized sofas and poolside beds to the attire of many of the conspicuously wealthy guests, it’s a busy vision in what lovers of the fashion brand will recognise as “Maiolica”, its distinctive patterned design.
These ultra-high-net-worths aren’t here to buy clothes, though. They are waiting to put their name down for Europe’s first Dolce & Gabbana residences, which are due to be completed in 2026. “This very special project, this very special experience, is the new Dolce & Gabbana lifestyle in Marbella,” says Domenico Dolce, one half of the world-famous fashion duo. title: Top 5 Insurance Coverage for Homeowners | DarGlobal
text:
Owning a home is a significant achievement and a substantial investment that necessitates protection. As a homeowner, it’s crucial to understand the various types of insurance coverage available to safeguard your property and finances. Here are five essential types of insurance coverage every homeowner should consider:
1. Homeowners Insurance
This is the most fundamental and necessary form of insurance for homeowners. It covers the structure of your home, your personal belongings, and liability protection in case someone is injured on your property. Homeowners insurance typically covers damage from fires, storms, theft, and other common hazards. However, it’s important to read the fine print, as certain natural disasters like floods and earthquakes are often not covered.
2. Flood Insurance

title: Top 5 Insurance Coverage for Homeowners | DarGlobal
text:
However, it’s important to read the fine print, as certain natural disasters like floods and earthquakes are often not covered.
2. Flood Insurance
Standard homeowners insurance policies do not cover flood damage. If your home is in a flood-prone area, flood insurance is indispensable. This insurance covers damage to your home’s structure and belongings due to flooding. The National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) and private insurers provide this coverage, which can be a lifesaver in safeguarding your investment against unpredictable natural disasters.
3. Earthquake Insurance
Similar to flood insurance, earthquake insurance is a must-have if you live in an area prone to earthquakes. This coverage helps repair or rebuild your home and replace personal belongings in the event of an earthquake. Considering the devastating impact an earthquake can have, this insurance provides essential financial protection.
4. Umbrella Liability Insurance

title: Top 5 Insurance Coverage for Homeowners | DarGlobal
text:
Considering the devastating impact an earthquake can have, this insurance provides essential financial protection.
4. Umbrella Liability Insurance
Umbrella liability insurance provides additional liability coverage beyond what your standard homeowners insurance offers. The first step in your luxury home buying journey is to take a comprehensive look at your financial health. This means evaluating your income, savings, investments, and credit score. Ancient Origins
Marbella's roots trace back to Roman times, with archaeological evidence suggesting settlements as early as the 7th century BC. The Moors, who ruled the region for centuries, left their mark with the charming old town's labyrinthine streets, the 10th-century castle walls, and the fragrant orange trees that grace the Plaza de los Naranjos.
Industrial Interlude
In the 19th century, Marbella experienced an unexpected industrial boom with the discovery of iron ore in the nearby hills. The city became a major producer of iron and steel, attracting workers and entrepreneurs from across Spain. While this industrial era ultimately faded, it left a lasting impact on Marbella's infrastructure and development.
The Rise of Tourism
In the mid-20th century, Marbella's picturesque coastline, year-round sunshine, and rich cultural heritage caught the eye of international travellers. This involves a collaborative process between the developer, architect, designer, and most importantly, the buyer.
The journey begins with a deep understanding of the buyer's lifestyle, preferences, and aspirations. The goal is to translate the buyer's vision into a tangible reality, a home that feels uniquely theirs.

title: Top 5 Attractions in Ras Al Khaimah | DarGlobal
text:
In the northernmost part of the United Arab Emirates, Ras Al Khaimah (RAK) is a hidden gem waiting to be discovered. Known for its rich history, stunning landscapes, and diverse attractions, RAK offers a unique blend of tradition and modernity that appeals to all types of travelers. Whether you're an adventure enthusiast, a history buff, or someone looking to relax, Ras Al Khaimah has something for you. In this blog, we will explore five top attractions that make this emirate a must-visit destination.
1. Jebel Jais – The Highest Peak in the UAE
Jebel Jais, part of the Hajar Mountain range, is the highest peak in the UAE, standing at 1,934 meters. It offers breathtaking views and a variety of activities for adventure seekers. The Jebel Jais Flight, the world's longest zipline, is a thrilling experience that lets you soar at speeds of up to 150 km/h over the stunning landscape. For those who prefer a more relaxed experience, the Jebel Jais Viewing Deck Park provides multiple terraces from which to enjoy panoramic views of the mountains and valleys.

title: Top 5 Attractions in Ras Al Khaimah | DarGlobal
text:
relaxed experience, the Jebel Jais Viewing Deck Park provides multiple terraces from which to enjoy panoramic views of the mountains and valleys.
Hiking enthusiasts will find numerous trails varying in difficulty, offering a chance to explore the rugged beauty of the Hajar Mountains. The cooler temperatures at the summit provide a refreshing escape from the heat of the lowlands, making Jebel Jais a perfect year-round destination.
2. Al Hamra Village and Al Hamra Mall
Al Hamra Village is a picturesque residential community that offers visitors a glimpse of luxury living in Ras Al Khaimah. With its pristine beaches, world-class golf course, and a range of dining and entertainment options, Al Hamra Village is a haven for relaxation and leisure. The Al Hamra Golf Club, designed by Peter Harradine, is an 18-hole championship course that caters to golfers of all skill levels.

text:

Adjacent to the village is Al Hamra Mall, a premier shopping destination in RAK. The mall features a wide variety of international and local brands, a multiplex cinema, and an array of dining options to suit all tastes. Whether you're looking to shop, dine, or simply unwind, Al Hamra Village and Al Hamra Mall have something for everyone.
3. Dhayah Fort – A Journey into History
For history enthusiasts, a visit to Dhayah Fort is a must. This 16th-century mud-brick fort is perched on a hilltop and offers a fascinating glimpse into the region's past. Dhayah Fort played a significant role in the resistance against British forces in the early 19th century and is the last hilltop fort still standing in the UAE.
The climb to the top of the fort rewards visitors with stunning views of the surrounding date palm oasis, the Arabian Gulf, and the rugged mountains. The fort's strategic location and historical significance make it a compelling destination for those interested in the rich cultural heritage of Ras Al Khaimah.

4. Ras Al Khaimah National Museum
Located in a historic fort that once served as the residence of the ruling family, the Ras Al Khaimah National Museum offers an in-depth look at the emirate's history and culture. The museum's exhibits include archaeological finds, traditional weapons, manuscripts, and artifacts that highlight the region's maritime heritage, pearl diving history, and traditional way of life.
One of the museum's highlights is the Qawasim Room, which displays documents and treaties between the rulers of Ras Al Khaimah and the British government, shedding light on the emirate's pivotal role in regional history. The museum also features a section dedicated to traditional Emirati architecture and an array of ethnographic exhibits that provide insight into the daily lives of the local people.
5. Al Wadi Nature Reserve – A Desert Oasis

5. Al Wadi Nature Reserve – A Desert Oasis
For nature lovers, the Al Wadi Nature Reserve offers a unique opportunity to explore the natural beauty of the desert landscape. Spanning 1,235 acres, this protected reserve is home to a variety of wildlife, including Arabian oryx, gazelles, and an array of bird species. The reserve's diverse ecosystems, from sand dunes to lush wadis, provide a haven for wildlife and a tranquil escape for visitors.
Guests can embark on guided nature walks, bird-watching tours, and wildlife safaris to learn more about the flora and fauna of the region. The reserve also offers activities such as archery, horseback riding, and falconry, providing a unique blend of adventure and education. The luxurious Ritz-Carlton Al Wadi Desert Resort, located within the reserve, offers world-class accommodations and amenities, making it an ideal base for exploring this natural wonder.

Spain's attractive tax regime, particularly for high-net-worth individuals, is a key factor driving investment in Marbella villas for sale.
Spain's income tax rates are generally lower than those in many other European countries, making it an attractive destination for those seeking to minimise their tax burden. Non-residents who become tax residents in Spain can benefit from the "Beckham Law," a special tax regime that allows them to be taxed as non-residents for their first six years in the country. This means they pay a flat rate of 24% on their income up to €600,000, with any income exceeding that threshold taxed at 47%.
In a move to attract wealthy individuals and encourage investment, the Andalusian regional government (where Marbella is located) has eliminated wealth tax as of 2023. This means that residents of Andalusia no longer have to pay an annual tax on their worldwide assets, making it an even more attractive location for high-net-worth individuals seeking to establish residency.

Residential real estate comes with many advantages for both new and experienced investors:
Consistent Demand For Housing: Everyone needs a home, which provides steady demand and ensures rental revenue and property appreciation.

A property insurance premium is a yearly amount that you pay to an insurance company for a policy that protects your real estate investment against various risks like fire, theft, and natural disasters. It is the cost of your financial protection plan.
The premium is your share of a risk pool, where insurance companies gather money from property owners and then use the collected funds to compensate for losses after a disaster. Your particular premium expresses a combination of the risk profile of your property and the selected coverage level.

To identify the areas where the risk is, insurance companies rely on the weather trends and the history of claims made in the area.
Property Characteristics: The age of the house, its size, the materials used for construction, and the architectural features are among the factors that have a direct impact on the calculations. Typically, a house that has been recently built with materials that are resistant to fire will be assigned a lower premium than an old property.

title: The Trains Are Coming: The GCC's Next Connectivity Leap
text:
In the late 1960s, Dubai Airport used to operate from 07:00 to 13:00, handling just a few hundred passengers a day.
After 13:15, the airport manager (more like a caretaker) would lock the doors and take the keys with him.
Today, Dubai moves more than 90M passengers a year, Abu Dhabi around 30M, and Doha over 50M — an extraordinary leap in one generation.
But as transformative as aviation has been for opening the Gulf to the world, the region is now entering a new era of mobility, driven by land connections within the GCC.
One rail announcement after another is transforming six separate markets into one connected region:
- Riyadh–Doha high-speed rail
~2 hours of travel, 10M+ passengers expected, 30K new jobs, ~$30B in economic impact.
- UAE domestic rail (Etihad Rail)
Linking 11 cities as of 2026. Abu Dhabi to Dubai in 57 minutes, with a future high-speed train cutting that to 30 minutes.
- UAE–Oman corridor (Hafeet Rail)
Connecting Abu Dhabi to Sohar in ~100 minutes, transforming both passenger movement and freight.
All of this feeds into the 2,100 km GCC Railway, which by 2030 aims to create a single passenger experience that feels like domestic travel.

When borders become this frictionless, behavior changes. Millions of air passengers now have tempting alternatives.
- Dubai residents can finish work on Friday and enjoy dinner in Muscat.
- Families in Doha see Riyadh as a two-hour weekend trip.
- Standalone trips evolve into multi-city Gulf experiences.
- Morning meetings in Riyadh, back in Abu Dhabi by afternoon.
- Supply chains reorganize around rail hubs.
- Companies hire across the GCC as commuting replaces relocation.
At this scale, mobility turns the GCC into one integrated economic system — because practically, it becomes one.
This vision for interconnectivity was laid down years ago:
- Saudi–Oman highway (2021)
Cut 16 hours of travel through the Empty Quarter.
- King Fahd Causeway (1986)
Linked Saudi Arabia and Bahrain and today moves 30M+ passengers a year.
These were early signals of a region thinking and acting as one. What’s different now is scale and timing: complementary systems being built simultaneously, with major links completing within this decade.

title: The Complete Guide to Investing in Dubai Off-Plan Properties
text:
Investing in real estate has consistently proven to be a cornerstone of global wealth creation, and few markets capture the imagination of international investors quite like Dubai. Renowned for its futuristic skyline, tax-free environment, robust infrastructure, and business-friendly policies, the emirate continues to attract capital from around the globe.
At the center of this real estate expansion is the market for Dubai off-plan property. Accounting for approximately 70% of residential real estate transactions, purchasing properties before or during their construction phase has transformed from a niche strategy into the primary engine driving Dubai's property landscape.
Whether you are an institutional investor seeking high rental yields or a first-time buyer looking for accessible entry points, understanding how to navigate the market for off-plan properties in Dubai is essential for maximizing your returns and minimizing risk.

When you buy an off-plan home, you are essentially committing to a property during its launch or early construction phase. In return for buying early, developers offer significant incentives, including lower entry prices compared to existing secondary market homes, interest-free payment schedules, and high capital growth potential before the keys are handed over.

One of the most appealing drivers of buying off-plan is the opportunity for early equity growth. Developers typically offer launch prices at a discount. As construction progresses through various stages, from foundation to structure and interior finishing, the market value of the unit naturally increases. Investors who buy at the initial launch often secure notable capital appreciation by the time handover occurs.
Unlike ready properties that require an immediate down payment of 20% to 25% alongside a full mortgage or cash payout, a Dubai off-plan property comes with developer-backed payment schedules. Common structures include:
- Construction-Linked Plans: Payments spaced out over construction milestones (e.g., 10% on booking, 60% during construction, 30% on handover).
- Post-Handover Payment Plans: Allowing buyers to pay a remaining percentage of the property price over 2 to 5 years after taking possession. This enables investors to fund payments using rental yield generated by the property.

Developments launched today feature modern architectural trends, energy-efficient designs, smart home technology, and top-tier community amenities. Modern off-plan projects feature resort-style infinity pools, co-working spaces, wellness hubs, and private parks, making them highly attractive to high-paying tenants upon completion.

- Project Registration Verification: Every legitimate project and developer receives an official registration number from RERA. Investors can verify these details online through the official Dubai REST mobile application.

The primary factor driving the value of a waterfront luxury property is fundamental economics: supply is strictly finite.
Developers can construct additional urban towers or extend suburban communities, but oceanfront and lakefront shorelines cannot be expanded. Because coastal land availability remains permanently capped, inventory stays limited. title: Capital Growth vs Rental Yield in Luxury Real Estate
text:
When building a high-value real estate portfolio, evaluating the trade-offs between capital growth and rental yield stands as one of the most critical steps in strategy development. Both metrics serve distinct roles in wealth generation, but in the luxury segment, they behave differently than in mass-market residential property.
Understanding how to balance long-term appreciation with immediate cash generation allows investors to optimize their total returns while managing risk across market cycles.
To construct an effective portfolio strategy, it is necessary to first separate how these two metrics generate financial value.
Capital Growth refers to the increase in a property’s market value over time. It represents the equity built between the original purchase price and the appreciated market value. In luxury real estate, capital appreciation is typically driven by geographic scarcity, architectural prestige, prime locations, and long-term infrastructure developments.

Rental Yield measures the annual income generated by a property as a percentage of its total purchase price or current market value. Standard valuation formulas often fall short because premium properties trade on emotional value, architectural distinction, and geographic exclusivity rather than strictly square footage.
To make a profitable acquisition, high-net-worth investors must separate superficial finishes from enduring asset value. Knowing how to properly evaluate luxury property assets requires looking beyond polished marble countertops and stage dressing to assess micro-market demand, architectural authorship, and long-term operating costs.
Location is the primary price driver in real estate, but at the luxury tier, performance is strictly hyperlocal. Two estates within the same neighborhood or even two units in the same high-rise can have drastically different valuations based on micro-factors.
